summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: PayPal CEO remakes team
articles.description: Chief Financial Officer Jamie Miller, who served as the digital payment company’s interim CEO at one point, will leave as CEO Enrique Lores installs new managers.

articles.title: Bill sells for $6B to TPG, Corpay
articles.description: The deal for the bill-pay company fuels consolidation in the business payments and receivables software industry.

articles.title: M&T aims to ‘dial up’ credit card rewards
articles.description: The regional lender is looking to offer simple and easy-to-understand credit card perks, in line with recent customer feedback.

articles.title: Researchers spot ACH loopholes
articles.description: University of Massachusetts academics have identified vulnerabilities that hackers could exploit in restricted bank accounts.

articles.title: Google wallet returns to Apple
articles.description: The wallet app gives Google an early lead among iPhone-wielding agentic shoppers and poses a rival for Stripe’s Link wallet, analysts said.

articles.title: ACI Worldwide’s CEO heads out
articles.description: Thomas Warsop is leaving the payments software company, with insiders taking over leadership until he’s replaced.

articles.title: Klarna launches AI ‘concierge’
articles.description: The buy now, pay later provider has waded into agentic commerce with a new tool and aims to expand its longer-term loan portfolio.

articles.title: Fed to boost payment service fees
articles.description: The Federal Reserve is also instituting a new access fee that it says will create a more “streamlined experience” for its bank clients.
